item: Interrupt safety follow-on to the gate swap (R161 R163 R165 R171): wait loops keep their back-edge inside the lock; four context managers give back what they took
summary: Real SIGALRM interrupts (about 49,500 per gate) found that a wait loop written `while wanted:` under a lock leaves the lock owned in 0.7 to 0.9 % of interrupts on CPython 3.13 (the back-edge sits outside the with's exception entry); the loops are now `while True: if not cond: break`, a dis-based test pins every one, and every loop a CLI reaches on the main thread (R163) is converted or on a named, call-graph-pinned worker-only allowlist (R165: event-loop rows are exempt because uvicorn captures SIGINT and SIGTERM, measured 18 of 18). R171: a scan of every context manager found 29 that take shared state before their try; 4 converted with red-without tests, swap_window converted (state left set in 7,013 of 30,872 interrupts before, 3,836 of 62,053 after, never the lock, all inside the cleanup functions themselves), 2 owed to the lanes that own the file, 23 allowlisted with a reason. The write gate joins its queue inside the try and releases by depth; the probe names where each interrupt landed. Full suite at 46ce6e548 (this branch plus a settings-lock detector that is NOT in this PR; 2026-10-17, started 06:40 UTC, 4 xdist workers, host otherwise idle): 23,587 passed, 214 skipped, 4 failed in 26 min 30 s; the four: test_gzip_flushes_every_chunk_of_a_streaming_response (fails on origin/main too, starlette below 1.5.0), the two tests/test_event_loop_signal_exemption.py tests that boot a real server and wait 60 s for it to be healthy (not healthy in 60 s with 4 workers running; both pass alone in 34 s), and one test of the detector's own, not in this PR. At this PR's head 6ddaf52d1 only the guards and the touched tests were run (1,773 passed); the full suite is CI's.
